messages:
maria: Quick sync — follow-up from the service-boundary RFC. We need to prioritize the top 3 slices for tech-debt paydown and decide migration strategies. Can we list the real blockers and a pragmatic rollforward plan?
elaine: +1, I can pull the hotspots from last quarter's incidents and perf dashboards.
raj: From infra side: the KV cache ownership still leaks across 3 services. That causes cascading evictions during bursts.
simon: Agree on the cache. Also the session-mesh proxy still handles auth enrichment for two different flows — duplication is painful.
tess: Two practical constraints: 1) business-critical low-latency hotpaths (chat/generation) can't take prolonged cutovers, 2) we need a small bounded team to own each extract.
maria: Proposal: (1) KV-cache extract as a dedicated slice with a thin adapter, (2) session-mesh auth enrichment -> sidecar consolidation, (3) surface shrink: split router + enrichers. Each with a 6-week plan and safety lifeboat.
elaine: For the KV slice, can we do a read-only read-through cache first, then swap writers? That reduces change blast radius.
raj: read-through makes sense. Implementation note: we'll need a migration flag and a feature toggle in the router. Example toggle usage: 
```yaml
feature_toggles:
  kv_migration_mode: gradual
  kv_primary: new-kv-service
  kv_fallback: legacy-cache
```
Start with 1% traffic, ramp to 100% over 2 weeks.
simon: On session-mesh: rather than immediate sidecar, run auth enrichment as a small service behind a facade so legacy paths can call it. Then replace instances with the sidecar via a canary.
tess: Risk register: list the things that could break: token expiry mismatch, race in kv write ordering, latency P95 increase. Need automated rollback triggers.
maria: Agreed. Rollback triggers (initial idea): P95 latency > 1.5x baseline for 5m, error-rate spike > 2x baseline, or end-to-end test failures. infra-bot: Deploy guard configured: p95_threshold=1.5, error_rate_multiplier=2.0, steady_window=300
elaine: Another operational ask — instrument per-route token-cost and per-model latency so we can localize regressions quickly. Put those metrics in the rollout dashboard.
raj: We'll also need a backward-compatible protobuf change for the adapter interface. Suggest additive fields only: 
```proto
message CacheRequest {
  string key = 1;
  bool prefer_new = 2; // optional, defaults false
}
```
Migration can read prefer_new and ignore when absent.
simon: Timeline suggestion: week 0-1 design & infra prep, week 2 implement read-through + toggle, week 3 start 1% ramp, week 4-5 monitor + ramp, week 6 cutover writers.
tess: Who's the owners? maria (project lead), raj (infra), elaine (obs + incidents), simon (api/adapter), plus 1 backend engineer per slice.
maria: I'll draft the sprint tasks and put a rough Gantt in the arch board. Action items: raj -> infra toggles + rollout dashboard by EOD Fri; elaine -> hotspots list and incident mapping by Monday; simon -> proto sketch & adapter plan by Wed; tess -> risk register + rollback playbook by Wed.
elaine: FYI, I pulled recent flakiness: two incidents trace to blobstore timeouts during cache warmups. We should include a blobstore fallback in the lifeboat.
raj: Good catch. We'll add a blobstore circuit with immediate fallback to legacy cache when latency > 200ms.
simon: Small dev note: keep the new adapter stateless so it can scale independently; persist nothing in-process.
tess: Also add a test harness that replays traffic slices for the 1% canary (same prompt distributions). That helped us catch a late tokenization regression last year.
maria: Thanks. I'll post the plan in the arch board and schedule a 30m sync Thurs to sign off. If no objections by then we'll spin up the infra tickets. :thumbsup:
